24832672cc.why: Fixed: 'most water left on its sunlit surface' and the context's polar cold-trap ice match NASA and Grokipedia. Key and wrong choices hold (escape speed 2.38 vs 11.2 km/s). No new tell; gravity-and-orbits keys the one-sixth pull, not air loss; no other final asks why the Moon has no air.

8db404346d.why: Fixed: asks the FIRST oxygen, so the old 'most of today's oxygen' overstatement is gone, and the land-plant lure means a T2 student who knows only that plants give off oxygen must also know microbes came first. Grokipedia: cyanobacteria in shallow marine settings, dissolved iron the first sink, build-up from about 2.43 billion years ago; land plants about 470 million years ago. Volcanoes and weathering give no free oxygen. No other final asks the Great Oxidation Event.

0cd8d44f8e.why: Fixed: the context now says 'most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet light' (ozone absorbs about 97-99 percent of harmful UV; UV-A passes). The stem and choices are unchanged and still true. elements-compounds-and-formulas mentions the ozone layer only in a context; no final keys it.

66f542351b.why: Fixed: the stem no longer says 'of the things the Sun sends out', and a space-rock lure breaks the three-kinds-of-light pattern. A field pushes only on charged particles, so light and neutral meteoroids are unchanged. The stem asks about the TOP of the air, so the 'more UV at the ground if ozone thinned' argument does not apply. The Mars stem 015179658a no longer pairs a lost field with the solar wind. The comets unit's solar-wind question keys comet tails, a different fact.

015179658a.why: Fixed: the stem asks what the solar wind 'does to the planet', so the air is no longer named before the key, and no stem or context links the solar wind to a magnetic field. MAVEN reached Mars orbit in September 2014; NASA 2015 gives about 100 g a second, and LASP 2017 reports most of the air lost. The wrong choices are not MAVEN findings. No other final asks MAVEN.

2cf96b1e28.why: Fixed: the cloud lure is now 'let most of the sunlight through', no longer an absolute and still false (Bond albedo about 0.77). Key: Venus's atmosphere is more than 10,000 times as massive as Mars's (OpenStax). The lead's greenhouse ruling keeps this question here. T1 keys only 'Venus is hottest'.

3ce51737b3.why: New question, true and in scope (habitability, not the T4 greenhouse mechanism). OpenStax: below 0.006 bar water's boiling point is as low as or lower than its freezing point, so liquid water cannot last even on a summer day above freezing. Massé et al. 2016 saw pure water boil on sediment at Martian pressure. Wrong choices: gravity is 38 percent of Earth's, a sol is about 24.66 h, and Martian wind pushes weakly (NASA). The choices are parallel ('Mars's X is so Y that...'), and the 'strong winds' lure (dust storms) stays live. No other final keys pressure and boiling point: T1 asks 100 C at sea level and T2 asks that salt raises the boiling point. Voice fine ('Suppose an astronaut').
